title: The Mirror of Fiction
text:
Metafiction is a form of writing that turns its attention inward, examining the conventions by which a story is constructed. Rather than hiding the author behind a seamless illusion, the text repeatedly reminds the reader that it is an artificial object. Such self-consciousness often produces a sense of vertigo, since the narrative cannot be trusted to stand on solid ground. Many readers initially find this unsettling before recognizing it as a source of intellectual pleasure.

The technique is not merely a playful gesture, however. By exposing its own machinery, metafiction invites a reflection on how reality itself is represented in language. A character may address the reader directly, or a narrator may admit that he has invented the events he describes. These moments dissolve the boundary between the world of the story and the world of the reader, leaving both uncertain of where fiction ends.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does metafiction direct the reader's attention toward?
options: The conventions by which a story is constructed.
The historical events that inspired the story.
The emotional lives of the characters.

questions.text: What examples does the second paragraph give of moments that blur the boundary between story and reader?
options: A character addresses the reader directly, or a narrator admits inventing the events.
A publisher alters the cover design, or a critic writes a review.
An editor cuts several chapters, or a library lends the book.
A translator adds footnotes, or a reader writes a letter.

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of metafiction?
options: It is merely a way of entertaining readers with tricks.
It is a serious way of questioning how reality is represented.
It is a technique that readers should avoid because it confuses them.
It is useful only in works of history.

questions.text: Why might the first paragraph describe the narrative as one that 'cannot be trusted to stand on solid ground'?
options: Because the story is set in an unstable historical period.
Because the text keeps revealing its own artificiality, undermining its authority.
Because the author deliberately changes the language between chapters.
Because the characters disagree about their memories.

vocabulary.definition: a feeling of dizziness or loss of stability, often used figuratively
causing worry, unease or lack of calm
to gradually disappear or break down
made by people rather than occurring naturally

paragraph_translations: Metaficção é uma forma de escrita que volta sua atenção para dentro, examinando as convenções pelas quais uma história é construída. Em vez de esconder o autor atrás de uma ilusão perfeita, o texto lembra repetidamente ao leitor que ele é um objeto artificial. Essa autoconsciência costuma produzir uma sensação de vertigem, pois a narrativa não pode ser considerada firme. Muitos leitores acham isso perturbador no início, antes de reconhecê-lo como uma fonte de prazer intelectual.

A técnica, porém, não é apenas um gesto lúdico. Ao expor sua própria engrenagem, a metaficção convida a refletir sobre como a própria realidade é representada na linguagem. Uma personagem pode dirigir-se diretamente ao leitor, ou um narrador pode admitir que inventou os acontecimentos que descreve. Esses momentos dissolvem a fronteira entre o mundo da história e o mundo do leitor, deixando ambos incertos sobre onde a ficção termina.
